  ],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the requested API changes, compatibility constraints, and unresolved migration and deletion decisions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"id": "K1", "applies": "yes"},

  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Who are the API callers, how does the runtime identify them, and do deletion or user records have visibility restrictions?",
      "changes": "Caller identity, authorization, confidentiality, and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the server and available project documentation; absent contrary evidence, callers are unidentified HTTP clients, the existing runtime supplies no authentication or per-user visibility, and no new identity system is assumed.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; claims of authenticated or restricted access require evidence."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "How should pagination be exposed while preserving the current unparameterized GET /users response?",
      "changes": "List behavior, query contract, and compatibility tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first establishes the existing endpoint and consumer contracts; absent a documented convention, retain the current array response without pagination parameters and treat pagination as opt-in.",
      "blocks": "The final pagination interface until discovery establishes any existing client expectations; the recorded default can otherwise proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What are the create and delete methods, paths, request fields, response bodies, status codes, and error shapes, including what 'same shape' means for each response?",
      "changes": "HTTP contracts and endpoint tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks existing endpoints, tests, and any project contracts; absent a stronger convention, use POST /users and DELETE /users/:id, preserve user fields id, name, and email, and interpret the list's shape as an array of user objects, with exact success and error details recorded before implementation.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing endpoint and response tests until the contract details are settled; the recorded defaults guide discovery."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What confirmation or other safeguard makes deletion sufficiently careful, and what happens for absent, invalid, repeated, or concurrently changed targets?",
      "changes": "Deletion safety, request contract, state transitions, and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks repository conventions and available requirements; absent a documented mechanism, require an explicit confirmation tied to the target ID and reject an unconfirmed delete without changing state.",
      "blocks": "The final delete contract and its tests until confirmation semantics and concurrent-change behavior are settled; the safety default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What page size and query validation apply, and how should empty, out-of-range, and short final pages behave?",
      "changes": "Pagination defaults, validation, and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks for an established page size and consumer convention; none is present in the inspected paginator, so assume a page size of 10, 1-based pages, and the existing paginator's result structure, correcting its short-page behavior.",
      "blocks": "Final pagination contract until discovery checks for an established convention; the recorded default otherwise proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Where should durable user data live, how is it initialized and recovered, and what happens on write failure, restart, and concurrent changes?",
      "changes": "Persistence design, data lifetime, failure handling, and restart and concurrency tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks deployment configuration and storage conventions; absent evidence, use a local durable file with the in-memory store as the running state, retain records across restarts, and do not claim multi-process coordination.",
      "blocks": "The durable storage location and failure contract until the runtime environment and write behavior are established; the single-process default otherwise proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What ID format, allocation, uniqueness, reuse, and migration rules does Kestrel require, including for existing users?",
      "changes": "ID generation, stored data, migration compatibility, and tests.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Discovery first seeks an authorized migration specification or owner and checks existing integer IDs; preserve existing IDs and avoid reusing deleted IDs, but record Kestrel compatibility as unverified rather than inventing its requirements.",
      "blocks": "A claim that IDs are Kestrel-compatible and any irreversible ID contract until authoritative migration requirements are found."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Are there deployment-specific runtime, port, or filesystem requirements beyond the repository's Node >=20, dependency-free setup and PORT-or-3000 behavior?",
      "changes": "Runtime configuration, persistence location, and delivery checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks project and environment configuration; otherwise retain Node >=20, built-in modules only, and the existing PORT override with port 3000 as the fallback.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the existing configuration is the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing store, paginator, and server seams must remain callable and independently testable as persistence and handlers are added?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries, exported interfaces, and test isolation.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks imports and tests; preserve the existing exported interfaces and keep storage, pagination, and HTTP handling separable.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the existing modules and exports provide the default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which checks prove unchanged existing responses, safe create and delete behavior, short-page pagination, and survival across a real restart?",
      "changes": "Acceptance checks and test coverage.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the existing tests and npm script; use node:test via npm test, with HTTP-boundary checks and a restart persistence check when implementation is authorized.",
      "blocks": "Completion of implementation verification until those checks run; no tests or server are started during intake."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Is a deployment target or access requirement specified anywhere beyond this folder?",
      "changes": "Delivery location, release steps, and access needs.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks available project delivery instructions; otherwise deliver the result in this project's source checkout and do not assume a deployment target or release authority.",
      "blocks": "A deployed outcome until a target, access, and release are established; source delivery can proceed under the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Are there specific security, data-protection, performance, or durability bounds beyond the existing service and careful deletion?",
      "changes": "Security and durability decisions and acceptance tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks project and deployment requirements; otherwise preserve existing access behavior, apply the explicit delete safeguard, and make no unsupported performance or security guarantees.",
      "blocks": "Claims of additional guarantees until their requirements are established; the recorded default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Which early checks expose the likely compatibility risks: changed GET responses, lost persisted data, incorrect final pages, unsafe deletion, and incompatible IDs?",
      "changes": "Risk-focused verification and delivery readiness.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first examines current behavior and migration evidence; use targeted contract, restart, partial-page, and deletion checks, and keep migration compatibility open until verified.",
      "blocks": "Final completion claims until the relevant checks and migration discovery are complete."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What do 'usual page size', 'careful', 'same shape', and Kestrel mean in this project, and what are the exact installed improve, parallel-work, and code-review procedures?",
      "changes": "Pagination, deletion, response contracts, ID compatibility, and required delivery workflow.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks project materials and the named installed skills; use the defaults in Q2-Q5 and Q7 where evidence is absent, and treat the host's skill descriptions as workflow leads rather than verified full instructions.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing the affected contracts and claiming completion of the requested workflows until their relevant evidence or recorded defaults are established."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the dependency-free Node users API in this folder, used through its HTTP server; this intake is read-only and starts no server or implementation.\\nS2 [fact and default]: Add creation and safeguarded deletion for HTTP callers; Q1, Q3, and Q4 assign discovery the identity, contract, and confirmation decisions, with explicit target-bound confirmation as the recorded safety default.\\nS3 [fact and default]: Support pagination without changing the existing unparameterized list response; discovery resolves Q2 and Q5, and inspection shows the paginator uses floor division, so a short final page is currently omitted and must be checked and corrected.\\nS4 [fact]: Keep the implementation simple and free of external dependencies, using the existing Node runtime requirements.\\nS5 [fact and default]: Keep users in memory while retaining changes across restarts; Q6 assigns discovery the storage and failure details, with local durable storage and a single-process assumption as defaults.\\nS6 [fact]: The later delivery workflow must run improve until it finds no substantive changes, fan tests and handler work out in parallel, and perform code review; Q14 assigns discovery of the named skills' exact procedures.\\nS7 [fact and open question]: Preserve IDs for the Kestrel migration; Q7 assigns discovery of authoritative ID requirements and blocks a compatibility claim until verified, while existing IDs remain unchanged by default. Discovery leads are the Kestrel migration team or owner, its workspace, channels, internal sites and documents, and any relevant private repository; these are unverified leads, not known locations, and sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/.\\nS8 [fact]: Preserve the server's existing PORT override and default port 3000; Q8 assigns discovery of any deployment-specific constraints.\\nS9 [fact and default]: Match the list endpoint's user representation for new responses; Q3 assigns discovery of whether its current array envelope is required for each operation, with the array interpretation recorded as the default.\\nS10 [fact and delivery boundary]: Preserve existing endpoint responses, including GET /users and GET /users/:id; the requested result must become usable in this project's source checkout after implementation and verification, while an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return and any deployed outcome exists only after release; no deployed target is named."
}
